newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela mulls "countercertifying" U.S. on drugs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mulls "countercertifying" U.S. on drugs.

text.p: Venezuela on Friday proposed "countercertification" of the United States in response to Washington's annual policy of certifying countries for their cooperation in the fight against drug trafficking.
"We will have to think of something, such as countercertification for example," Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Burelli Rivas told a news conference.
Burelli did not explain what he meant by countercertification.
The U.S. State Department certified Venezuela as an ally in the war against the narcotics trade in its annual review Feb. 28, but Burelli rejected the process as arbitrary and unfair.
Washington's evaluations provoked bitter reaction in many Latin American countries, particularly Colombia which was decertified for the second year running.
U.S. President Bill Clinton is scheduled to visit Venezuela during a tour of Latin American and Caribbean countries in May.
